title: Cao Cao Sings on the Yangtze and Kills a Man for Saying So
summary: The night before the battle Cao Cao holds a banquet on the water, takes a spear, and sings his own poem to the moon — 'the moon is bright, the stars are few, the crows fly south'. An officer remarks that crows flying south at night is an ill omen on the eve of a battle. Cao Cao runs him through with the spear, and goes on singing.
He apologises in the morning and buries him well.
history: The poem is Cao Cao's own and survives. The killing is the novel's, and it is placed here to remind you what he is on the night before he loses.

pins.note: Sings, and kills a man for listening carefully.
